title: Ollama GGUF quantization -- T1005 heap out-of-bounds read exfiltrated via model push
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-7482 (CVSS 8.8 HIGH), affecting
Ollama before 0.17.1.

The `/api/create` endpoint accepts an attacker-supplied GGUF model file.
During quantization (`fs/ggml/gguf.go` and `server/quantization.go`'s
`WriteTo()`), the server trusted the file's declared tensor offset and
size fields without validating them against the file's actual length.
A GGUF file whose declared offset/size exceeds the real file causes the
quantization path to read past the allocated heap buffer -- the leaked
memory can contain environment variables, API keys, system prompts, and
OTHER CONCURRENT USERS' conversation data. Because `/api/create` and
`/api/push` both ship with no authentication in the upstream
distribution, an attacker can chain the two: upload a malicious GGUF to
`/api/create` to trigger the overread, then push the resulting model
artifact -- now carrying the leaked heap bytes baked into it -- via
`/api/push` to an attacker-controlled registry, exfiltrating the memory
contents as an ordinary-looking model file. Default deployments bind to
loopback, but the documented `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` configuration is
widely used in practice.

Detection logic flags the two-endpoint sequence this exfiltration
chain depends on: a `/api/create` call carrying a GGUF payload followed
by a `/api/push` call targeting a registry host outside an
operator-approved allowlist, from the same source in a short window --
a legitimate model-authoring workflow rarely pushes to an unfamiliar
registry immediately after a fresh create call.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor fix (ollama/ollama, via the merged
PR and NVD's technical summary, which quotes the specific vulnerable
files and functions), fixed in 0.17.1 (validates tensor size against
the shape-derived expected size before quantization).
